cues.text: Eighty years ago, in San Francisco, fifty nations signed a charter that opened with three words. We the peoples.
cues.note: the field is still finding its shape; nothing on screen yet but dust

cues.text: Everything since has been an argument about whether we meant them.
cues.note: lands under the title block, before it lifts away

cues.text: We work for a President who has spent his life inside this system.
cues.note: his name has just resolved; the career list begins at 25.0

cues.text: A career diplomat. An academic. A United Nations official in New York and Geneva.
cues.note: the first three posts arrive at 25.0, 27.4 and 29.7 — UNCTAD is on screen

cues.text: Adviser to the interim government of Bangladesh. Then its Foreign Minister.
cues.note: those two land at 34.4 and 36.7

cues.text: And then elected by the Member States to preside over this Assembly.
cues.note: the last line of the list, in gold, at 39.1

cues.text: Every President chooses a theme. It is not a slogan. It is a job description.
cues.note: the career lifts away at 43; the theme headline resolves from 45

cues.text: Restoring trust. Managing transformation. A United Nations that delivers for all.
cues.note: runs a moment past the scene, landing under the first welcome words

cues.text: An office like this one is built from nothing, in a matter of weeks.
cues.note: the logo dissolves; the ring of scripts begins to arrive

cues.text: Strangers arrive from twenty-five countries and are asked, immediately, to work as one.
cues.note: the words are cycling through the office’s own languages

cues.text: So we start where the Assembly starts. With welcome.
cues.note: the words bloom together and hand over

cues.text: Nine teams — and not one of them can finish a day’s work without another.
cues.note: the second counter

cues.text: And twenty-five places we call home.
cues.note: the third counter, handing off to the globe

cues.text: This is where the people in this room come from.
cues.note: the nebula folds into the Earth

cues.text: Not an abstraction. A childhood. A first language. A reason someone came into this work.
cues.note: ignition begins — Canada first, then west to east

cues.text: Some of us come from countries that have sent hundreds of thousands of peacekeepers into other people’s wars.
cues.note: the Americas and West Africa are alight

cues.text: Some from islands so small the atlas leaves them out — and whose coastline is a running argument with the sea.
cues.note: literally true of this build: three of our nations need dots drawn by hand

cues.text: Some from countries sheltering more than a million people who could not go home.
cues.note: South Asia is lighting up

cues.text: Every one of them sends a line back to New York. Not one of us arrived here by accident.
cues.note: the arcs are the point of the scene

cues.text: Whatever the Assembly argues about this year, someone in this room has lived it.
cues.note: the last countries ignite; the camera starts to pull back

cues.text: Twenty-five nations. One Assembly.
cues.note: the closing card appears at 133

cues.text: Now the harder thing to put on a map. The people.
cues.note: the globe slides right; the first cards come in

cues.text: We are an intergenerational team.
cues.note: the first region’s cards are on screen

cues.text: Colleagues in their mid-twenties, working beside people who were negotiating in this building before the youngest of us were born.
cues.note: the sweep moves through the middle regions

cues.text: One brings the assumption that all of this could work better. The other knows exactly why it does not — and how to move it anyway.
cues.note: the point of the scene: neither half is the junior partner

cues.text: And there is no flag to defend at this desk. Only a hundred and ninety-three Member States who have to be able to trust us equally.
cues.note: the President’s own commitment: everyone’s President, without fear or favour

cues.text: Multilingualism is not decoration here. It sits in the President’s mandate, next to gender parity, geographic balance and accessibility.
cues.note: the word cloud rises out of the dust

cues.text: It is the difference between a delegation being heard and a delegation being handled.
cues.note: the cloud is at its fullest

cues.text: Nineteen languages, in one office.
cues.note: the number resolves at 205.6

cues.text: Five of the six official languages of the United Nations are already in this room.
cues.note: the on-screen line names them; the voice does not repeat the list

cues.text: Six pillars. This is the actual work.
cues.note: the first cards are landing

cues.text: Peace that is prevented rather than ended. Development that reaches the countries everyone else forgets.
cues.note: pillars I and II, as all six settle into place

cues.text: A planet we are holding in trust for people who are not born yet. Rights defended in the small places, close to home.
cues.note: pillars III and IV — Kofi Annan and Eleanor Roosevelt, both quoted in the vision statement

cues.text: Technology governed rather than merely adopted. And an Assembly willing to reform itself.
cues.note: pillars V and VI, on the hold before the cards lift

cues.text: Sixty-five per cent of this Office is women.
cues.note: the glyph field fills in

cues.text: In a system still arguing about who belongs at the peace table, that is worth saying.
cues.note: the legend appears at 248 — resolution 1325 is in the President’s first pillar

cues.text: Fourteen of us were sent to this work by our own governments — thirteen countries that could have kept their best people at home.
cues.note: the "how we came here" panel; no contract type is named anywhere, by request

cues.text: They work beside twenty colleagues of the United Nations itself. Different routes in. One Office.
cues.note: both figures on screen; the flags of the sending countries are landing

cues.text: Four of the five regional groups are already here. We speak for all five.
cues.note: the regional bloom opens at 264.3 — Eastern Europe is the group we are missing

cues.text: Hammarskjöld said this Organization was not built to bring us to heaven. It was built to save us from hell.
cues.note: the field is folding back into the mark

cues.text: That is the work. Welcome to the Office of the President of the General Assembly.
cues.note: the closing title reveals from 279.8

cues.text: Multilateralism is not only relevant. It is indispensable to a future of peace, dignity, and prosperity for all.
cues.note: the vision statement’s own last sentence, spoken over the held final card after the timeline has come to rest
